title: Unix, at the level you meet it
summary: Not a shell course and not systems administration: the handful of operating-system facts that decide how a Node process behaves once your terminal is not the thing starting it. What it inherits from whoever launched it, which of its two output streams a line belongs on, what a signal actually is and what has to happen before the platform stops waiting, and why the container runs as a number that has to match the one on the volume.
